Accounts¶

Views¶

Views for account registration, role routing, and user dashboards.

accounts.views.dashboard(request)[source]¶

Send each authenticated user to the dashboard for their selected role.

accounts.views.editor_dashboard(request)[source]¶

Display the dashboard for users with the Editor role.

accounts.views.journalist_dashboard(request)[source]¶

Display the dashboard for users with the Journalist role.

accounts.views.reader_dashboard(request)[source]¶

Display the dashboard for users with the Reader role.

accounts.views.register(request)[source]¶

Create a Reader, Journalist, or Editor account and sign it in.

accounts.views.role_required(role)[source]¶

Restrict a view to a single application role (superusers are allowed).

Models¶

Custom user model for the News Application.

The application uses a single CustomUser model with a role field for Reader, Editor, and Journalist accounts.

Role-specific relationships are represented using Django relationships, including subscriptions for readers and authored content for journalists. This keeps authentication simple while supporting role-based behaviour.

class accounts.models.CustomUser(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: AbstractUser

Extends Django’s AbstractUser with a role field and role-specific subscription fields.

approved_articles¶

Accessor to the related objects manager on the reverse side of a many-to-one relation.

In the example:

class Child(Model):
    parent = ForeignKey(Parent, related_name='children')

Parent.children is a ReverseManyToOneDescriptor instance.

Most of the implementation is delegated to a dynamically defined manager class built by create_forward_many_to_many_manager() defined below.

save(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Enforce the brief’s rule: “If a user has a Journalist role, the program should assign the fields for the reader a value of ‘None’, and vice versa.”

ManyToMany fields cannot be set before the row has a primary key, so the M2M clearing happens in the post_save signal (accounts/signals.py) which runs after this save() completes.
